body:
## 3. The R&D map, the ML research brief, and ever-gauzy findings

### 3a. Sunday Frontier R&D Map (2026-07-05)

Source: `docs/research/SUNDAY_FRONTIER_R_AND_D_MAP_2026-07-05.md`. Purpose: identify aggressive but
**lawful** research and implementation lanes. Standing operating rule: phrase "loopholes" as lawful
openings, terms-approved gaps, open-source analogs, public-data methods, underused rights-cleared
sources, competitor blind spots, workflow asymmetries, and process advantages.

**Legal boundary — allowed:** open datasets; public documentation; terms-approved APIs; cleared
first-party data; open-source methods; academic formulas; synthetic fixtures; derived metrics from
cleared inputs; local-only shadow architecture; public-safe media, docs, and tests; guardrails that
block unsupported claims.
**Not allowed:** restricted scraping; paywall bypass; CAPTCHA bypass; credential misuse; fake
accounts; proprietary formula copying; raw paid API redistribution; raw NGS row exposure;
copyrighted broadcast footage without rights; live AWS or paid resources without approval; fake
performance, revenue, audience, or sponsor claims; auto-publishing, auto-emailing, or betting automation.
**Requires owner or counsel approval:** live data contracts; affiliate/sportsbook offers; public API
terms; public performance claims; use of benchmark data with uncertain redistribution rights; any AWS
deploy, account mutation, or paid service.

**Open data and rights-cleared inputs:** nflverse and other open football data for historical features
and validation; public schedules, rosters, depth charts, injuries, snap counts, play-by-play where
licenses permit; synthetic fixtures for partner collaboration, AWS mocks, and API payload tests;
user-provided private data in local-only tools, with payload-rights classification before any export.
Research objective: turn raw facts into GSE-derived features, expected baselines, residuals,
uncertainty, and decision-quality scores. **Never re-serve raw restricted feeds as the product.**

**Academic and open methods (high-value, to explore):** proper scoring rules (Brier, log loss,
calibration error, sharpness); conformal prediction for uncertainty intervals; Elo, Glicko,
TrueSkill for latent strength baselines; Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce for matchup comparisons;
hierarchical Bayes and empirical Bayes shrinkage for sparse player/team samples; Kalman filters
and state-space models for time-varying form; hidden Markov models for role and usage regimes;
splines and generalized additive models for nonlinear feature effects; hurdle and Tweedie models
for zero-inflated fantasy or yardage outcomes; model parliament with vetoes and disagreement
tracking; drift detection with PSI, KL divergence, chi-square, ECE drift, segment parity.
Engineering requirement: **every method must become a deterministic, tested, documented shadow
primitive before it can influence public claims.**

**Prediction and decision research — priority questions:** (1) What does the model think will
happen? (2) How calibrated is that probability? (3) How reliable are the inputs? (4) How stale
or contradictory is the market? (5) What is the no-bet pressure? (6) What would make the decision
wrong? (7) What can be shown publicly without leaking protected weights or restricted payloads?

**Decision doctrine:** Confidence is not win probability. GSE Signal Score is decision quality,
not win probability. No bet is a decision. High EV cannot override missing data, stale inputs,
unclear rights, drift, or calibration debt.

**Market intelligence — lawful lanes:** derived market movement summaries from terms-approved odds
inputs; stale-line risk scoring; book dispersion scoring; playable-window scoring; market mirage
detection from open or licensed snapshots; synthetic market fixtures for tests and public education.
**Do not:** claim market-beating performance without settled evidence; imply CLV success without
sample size and approval; expose raw paid odds payloads if terms do not allow it.

**Source rights and payload rights — required architecture:** source-rights envelope for every data
input; payload-rights classification for every API response; metric birth certificate for every
proprietary metric; metric card, model card, validation report, and drift card before promotion;
public/private exposure level on every metric. Immediate lane: adapters under
`apps/web/lib/source-rights` and `apps/web/lib/ip` reusing the existing registry and
prediction-engine metric rights primitives; tests that restricted, unclear, stale, and raw-payload
inputs fail closed.

**API readiness — safe API product:** GSE-derived intelligence only; no raw sports data resale; no
raw odds resale; no raw NGS exposure; auth required; scopes required; rate limit required;
request ID required; response envelope required; payload-rights filter required; usage event
required; raw keys never logged.

**Media and commercial growth — best lawful asymmetry:** show the operating system, not fake
certainty; teach why sports prediction needs audits; turn losses into autopsies; make no-bet
discipline visible; explain source reliability and stale-market failure modes; create partner
trust with disclosure and editorial independence. Guardrail: every public title, hook, script,
sponsor package, and offer copy should pass commercial-copy and unsupported-performance scans
before publication.

**AWS and cloud shadow R&D:** AWS is support infrastructure, not the center of the company.
No-cost lanes: Shadow Control Tower governance fixtures; Well-Architected six-pillar scorecards;
Bedrock/AgentCore agent contracts as local specs; Bedrock Guardrails policy blueprints as local
docs; SageMaker Model Monitor analogs through local model/drift cards; Clean Rooms synthetic
collaboration fixtures; Step Functions ASL fixtures for metric validation workflows; EventBridge
event fixtures for audit and drift events; CDK synth fixtures only. **No live AWS action:** no
credentials, no deploy, no account mutation, no hosted resources, no DNS, no paid service.
Funding/credits candidates to verify from official pages before action: AWS Activate, Google
Cloud for Startups, Microsoft for Startups, NVIDIA Inception, DigitalOcean Hatch or startup
programs, Neon startup or launch programs, Databricks startup programs, Vercel startup or
credits options. (This pass did not live-refresh those program terms — any application packet
must verify current eligibility, obligations, credit expiration, and data/security terms first.)

**Next experiments (the 10):** (1) partner-offer compliance scanner with high-risk
sportsbook/DFS fail-closed defaults; (2) API payload-rights scanner blocking raw NGS, raw paid
odds, restricted-source echoes; (3) source-rights adapters reusable across content, API, metric,
model surfaces; (4) no-bet governor tests proving stale inputs, calibration debt, drift, missing
data can veto high EV; (5) metric backlog slice: Receiver Difficulty and Expected YAC with birth
certificates, protected transforms, directional tests; (6) Well-Architected local scorecard index
under `docs/aws`; (7) 30-day media queue fixture with claim-safety scores and public-safe CTAs;
(8) API auth pure seam with hashed key comparison and no raw-key logging tests; (9) model/drift
card generator for every shadow metric asset; (10) commercial page visual QA and route smoke
after copy updates.

**Success metrics:** more repo-visible proof, fewer unsupported claims; more tests around trust
boundaries; every commercial surface has claim-safety gates; every proprietary metric has birth
certificate and rights envelope; every API proposal has payload-rights classification; every AWS
artifact remains local, no-cost, credential-free; every public claim can point to code, docs,
tests, or settled evidence.

### 3b. Machine learning research brief (2026-09-18)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-18-ml-research-brief.md`. Written as a self-contained prompt for an
outside research agent to redesign the prediction core.

**The honest current-state brief it carries:** prediction is a hand-weighted additive score
(consensus, book depth, edge, line movement, rest, form, venue, summed with fixed caps) measured
**anti-predictive at the top of its range**: picks scored 80+ claim ~87% and realize ~52%. Beneath
it sit market-blind independent estimators (Elo, Poisson, Dixon-Coles, Skellam, Bradley-Terry
standings model, opponent-adjusted EPA) that on football frequently collapse to a single source.
The only component measured well calibrated is the de-vigged market consensus probability. Free
data: nflverse play-by-play 1999–present (EPA, WP, CPOE, air yards); Next Gen Stats weekly
aggregates; injuries, snap counts, depth charts, rosters, officials, contracts; multi-book odds
with an append-only line-snapshot archive; weather; MLB Statcast; public exchange prices.
Paid charting and grade data exists but is not licensed. Sample sizes: ~2,600 settled picks
total, ~70 ever settled for the NFL, spread across sports, markets, seasons. CLV ~23% beat-close
vs 52.4% target. Product premise: never overstates its own accuracy — any method that cannot
state honest uncertainty is unusable regardless of accuracy.

**The ML regime (evaluate every method against this explicitly):** (1) extremely low
signal-to-noise — single-game outcomes near-coin-flips, edges worth having are 1–3 percentage
points; (2) an adversarial, highly efficient price — the closing line is a strong aggregator of
all public information; beat it, not merely predict outcomes; (3) small and unevenly distributed
samples, thinnest where we most want them; (4) non-stationarity — rules, rosters, coaching,
market efficiency all drift; (5) severe leakage hazards — play-level rows dependent within a
drive/game, post-game info contaminates retrospective features, in-play prices encode partial
outcomes; (6) heterogeneous, irregularly sampled, missing-heavy inputs; (7) calibration and
honest abstention matter more than raw accuracy. A method that wins on large-sample benchmarks
and fails here is a negative result — report it as one.

**The 15 research areas** (each: what it is, strongest published evidence for/against in sports
or analogous low-signal market-pricing domain, build cost on the listed data, realistic
magnitude of improvement, failure modes, a falsifiable kill criterion to abandon it):
1. Tabular learners — LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost vs regularized linear models in low-SNR
   small-n; monotonic constraints, quantile objectives, early stopping under dependent folds. Is
   the published boosting advantage real at our sample sizes or an artifact of large benchmarks?
2. Hierarchical partial pooling and multi-task learning — the direct attack on small n: share
   strength across sports, markets, seasons, teams so a 70-row stratum borrows from a 2,000-row
   one. Hierarchical Bayes, mixed-effects, empirical Bayes shrinkage, multi-task nets,
   meta-learning. Which formulation is best supported and how is the shrinkage schedule chosen
   rather than guessed?
3. Representation learning on play-by-play — self-supervised pretraining on decades of plays
   (next-play prediction, masked play modeling, contrastive drive embeddings), then fine-tune
   for outcome. Has anyone demonstrated transfer to outcome or market-beating prediction? Include
   tracking-data work and Big Data Bowl literature. Be explicit about whether available scale
   supports pretraining at all and what scaling behavior has actually been observed.
4. Sequence and state-space models for team strength — Kalman filters, particle filters,
   dynamic Elo, Gaussian processes over time, temporal fusion transformers. How should latent
   strength evolve and how is process noise fit rather than assumed?
5. Learning to rank and selection, not just probability — publishing is a ranking/selection
   problem. Listwise/pairwise objectives, LambdaMART, top-k under budget, learning to abstain,
   selective prediction with coverage-risk curves.
6. Inherently interpretable high-capacity models — explainable boosting machines and GA2M,
   neural additive models, GAMs with pairwise interactions, monotone constrained ensembles. Do
   they close the accuracy gap, and do per-feature contributions hold up as real explanations?
   Contrast with post-hoc attribution (SHAP, integrated gradients) and report known critiques
   honestly.
7. Uncertainty and calibration — conformal prediction, Mondrian and cross-conformal variants,
   Venn-Abers multiprobability, conformalized quantile regression, adaptive conformal under
   shift. What guarantees survive when exchangeability is violated by drift? Smallest honest
   calibration set? When is refusal the correct answer?
8. Market-relative learning — model the closing price as baseline, learn only the residual.
   Beat-the-close as training target vs outcome. Line movement, steam, order-flow features. What
   does market microstructure literature say about when a public model can persistently beat a
   liquid close, and in which markets/sports that has actually been demonstrated?
9. Online learning and non-stationarity — follow-the-regularized-leader, exponentially weighted
   forecaster aggregation, online gradient descent on proper scoring rules, contextual bandits,
   change-point detection, drift-aware retraining. Regret bounds that mean something at our
   data rate.
10. Causal inference — double/debiased ML, uplift modeling, synthetic controls, causal forests.
    Where does causal framing genuinely beat predictive (injury impact, coaching change, rest)
    and where is it overkill?
11. Ensembling and distillation — stacking, Bayesian model averaging, mixture of experts with
    learned router over sport/market, distilling a large ensemble into a deployable model. How
    are experts and routers fit without overfitting the router at our sample sizes?
12. Automated discovery — automated feature engineering, symbolic regression, neural architecture
    search, LLM-driven hypothesis generation. Report honestly: most have weak track records on
    low-signal tabular problems, and an earlier internal symbolic-regression effort produced no
    surviving finding.
13. Multimodal and heterogeneous fusion — structured stats + text (news, beat reports, injury
    language) + weather grids + market ticks. Early vs late fusion, missing-data-aware
    architectures, text embeddings as features, and whether text has ever added information
    beyond the price in a liquid sports market.
14. Frontier-model techniques that transfer — evaluate each for real applicability, not
    metaphor: retrieval augmentation (similar historical games as context), test-time compute and
    self-consistency, mixture of experts, curriculum and data ordering, distillation,
    preference/reward modeling trained on realized outcomes, critic and verifier models as a
    veto layer, scaling-law analysis for how much more data actually buys, continual learning
    without catastrophic forgetting.
15. **The learning loop as system design — "may be the most important section."** How do
    serious ML organizations build systems that improve continuously? Feature stores and
    point-in-time correctness, automated backtesting with purged and embargoed
    cross-validation, champion/challenger promotion, shadow deployment, experiment tracking and
    pre-registration, multiple-hypothesis control across candidate features, data versioning and
    reproducibility, automated monitoring for drift and calibration decay, active learning for
    what to label next. The reference architecture and the failure modes that make loops stall.

**Framing correction behind the brief:** large models do not improve because of the
transformer. They improve because a loop runs continuously and automatically: data lands, the
model trains, an eval scores it, the winner deploys, the deployment produces more data. Every
component of that loop already exists in this repository and none of it is wired to run.

**Evidence standard (non-negotiable):** cite primary sources (title, authors, venue, year, link
or DOI actually seen); if a citation cannot be verified, write UNVERIFIED rather than presenting
it as established — a fabricated citation makes the whole report unusable. Separate explicitly
for every claim: demonstrated in a sports/market-pricing setting with out-of-sample results;
demonstrated only in other domains; plausible but untested. Report effect sizes with sample
sizes and whether evaluation used a proper time-ordered split. Report negative results and
replication failures — as valuable as positives, harder to find. Where a claimed edge exists,
ask whether it would survive the vig, and say so.

**Deliverable format:** executive summary ≤1 page (three things that would most improve the
engine + three seductive approaches to refuse); one section per research area; a ranked build
list (each item: expected improvement, data required, engineering cost, sample size needed
before evaluation is possible at all, pre-registered kill criterion, dependencies); a proposed
reference architecture for the continuous learning loop concrete enough to implement (with
schedule); an explicit list of what could not be determined and what would resolve it.

**Anti-goals:** do not recommend deep learning because it is modern; do not recommend a method
without saying how it fails; do not treat accuracy as the objective when the objective is
calibrated probability plus beating a price; do not propose anything requiring data we cannot
lawfully use; do not pad with definitions of well-known methods.

**Admission rule (how a report's recommendations enter the engine):** through the same door as
every other signal — a pre-registered hypothesis with a kill line written on the same line as
the prediction, a shared test set, fixture-grouped and time-ordered folds, and a result recorded
whether it lives or dies. A method that cannot pass that door is research, not product,
however impressive its provenance.

### 3c. ever-gauzy as reference architecture (2026-09-18)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-18-ever-gauzy-reference-architecture.md`. Read at the founder's
request, scoped to two questions: monorepo structure and multi-tenancy. Source:
`ever-co/ever-gauzy`, public, cloned shallow; every claim checked in that tree.

**Monorepo:**
| | ever-gauzy | GSE |
|---|---|---|
| Packages | 36 across `apps/*`, `packages/*`, `packages/plugins/*`, `tools` | 25 across `apps/*`, `packages/*`, `workers/*` |
| Tooling | Nx plus Lerna plus Yarn 1 classic | npm workspaces, no orchestrator |
| Boundary enforcement | Nx project graph and tags | none today |

The pattern worth taking (already converged on): Gauzy puts every shared interface in
`packages/contracts`, a dependency-free package everything else imports — exactly the role
`@sports/types` plays. Rule to make explicit: anything both `apps/web` and `packages/*` need
crosses through `@sports/types`; it takes no dependency on either side. What not to take:
Nx+Lerna+Yarn1 (three overlapping tools; Yarn 1 EOL). At 25 packages npm workspaces is
adequate. The one capability Nx buys that GSE lacks: a machine-checked dependency graph that
would turn "`packages/*` never imports `apps/web`" into a build error rather than a convention —
cheap close is an enumerating test, not an Nx migration.

**Multi-tenancy — the finding that matters, and it argues against adopting Gauzy's approach:**
isolation is NOT automatic in Gauzy. No query-level guard, no row-level security, no ORM
middleware scoping reads. Enforcement is `RequestContext.currentTenantId()`, read off the
current user and called manually across **196 files**, with **42 sites** writing
`tenantId: RequestContext.currentTenantId()` into a where clause by hand. A single forgotten
`tenantId` on a single query is a cross-tenant read, and neither the type system nor the
database prevents it.

GSE's verified position (`packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`): **single-tenant**. No `Tenant`,
`Organization`, or `Workspace` model; zero occurrences of `tenantId`, `organizationId`,
`workspaceId`. The one signal toward future need: `packages/partner-stack` (`assessPartner`,
`grantCredits`, `allowedRevenueStreams`, `REVENUE_STREAMS`, `BLOCKED_PARTNER_KINDS`) — partner
revenue scaffolded, not live, one importer outside its own directory.

**Corrected recommendation:** "do not build multi-tenancy now" was wrong — it treated a product
decision not yet made as a reason to defer foundational work whose cost only rises with time.
**Build the foundation now; gate the product decision separately.** Retrofitting a tenant key is
a function of how much data and how many customers exist when you do it; today every row belongs
to one tenant by definition, so the backfill is a constant and every migration is reversible.
GSE's measured advantage: ONE database client export (`packages/db/src/index.ts:250`), imported
by 240 files (221 outside tests) — a central chokepoint where two fail-CLOSED layers can be
enforced: Postgres row-level security so the database refuses cross-tenant rows, plus a Prisma
client extension at the single `db` export. Neither depends on a developer remembering anything.

**The hazard that decides the design:** pooled connections (`packages/db/src/index.ts:225-233`
builds a Neon Pool) — a session-level `SET app.current_tenant` leaks the previous request's
tenant into the next one on a reused connection. Every assignment must be transaction-local,
inside an explicit transaction, issued as `SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant', $1, true)` —
`SET LOCAL` has the same lifetime but takes no bind parameter, so only `set_config` can carry
the tenant as a bound argument rather than interpolated SQL. 33 non-test `$transaction` call
sites already exist, so the pattern is established.

**Queued:** `docs/ops/hermes/BUILD-QUEUE-2026-09-18-tenancy.md` (six tasks): merged and deployed
with no founder action, nothing behaves differently — a pure tenancy library in `@sports/types`,
a tested client extension attached to nothing, two SQL proposals the founder applies on his own
schedule, an enumerating guard committed skipped with a named unskip condition, a cutover
runbook. The remaining founder decision is narrower: **which tables are tenant-scoped** (the
queue classifies each of the 102 models three ways and escalates the ambiguous set); if
white-label is never a path, phase one simply is not applied and the foundation sits on the
shelf at zero running cost.

**Not examined (scoped out):** their plugin architecture, desktop app packages, MCP server
package, auth model beyond the tenant accessor, migration strategy, test approach.

---

title: NFL-RevEng-KB | 4. Scraping and competitor-intel lessons (scrape-wave-2 + competitor-scrape) [Pre-September-17 Research Digest — NFL Analytics Reverse-Engineering Knowledge Base]
body:
## 4. Scraping and competitor-intel lessons (scrape-wave-2 + competitor-scrape)

### 4a. Scrape wave 2 — what to pull next

Source: `docs/research/scrape-wave-2.md`. Run list through the same Firecrawl prompt as wave 1
(`docs/research/competitor-scrape-2026-09-12.md` has the prompt and wave-1 results), prioritized
by what the factor engine and projections table were actually waiting on.

**Tier 1 — the factor engine was blocked on these:**
1. `baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_leaderboard` (batters, 2025) — full table: barrel%,
   hard-hit%, EV50, LA SwSp%, exit velo avg, distance avg per player → the `underlying`
   factor input for every MLB pick.
2. `baseballsavant.mlb.com/leaderboard/statcast` (pitchers, 2025) — plus spin rate, whiff%,
   chase% → pitcher-side `underlying`.
3. `fangraphs.com/projections.aspx` — ATC, THE BAT, Steamer, ZiPS model families and weights;
   projection numbers per player to compare against ours.
4. `propfinder.app/nfl` (logged in) — sign-in gate blocked wave 1; need the cheatsheets: TD,
   rushing, redzone, line, coverage matchup data → `matchupSplit` factor.
5. `prizepicks.com/` or `underdogfantasy.com/` — public pick percentages per prop; the
   over/under split for the `consensus` factor (5,000-over / 3,700-under).

**Tier 2 — makes the optimizer and props board real:**
6. `linestarapp.com/Props` (logged in) — actual Recent Form numbers (L5, L10, Season, Last LG)
   and Matchup+ Imp values.
7. `linestarapp.com/Ownership` (logged in) — Proj Own % vs Actual Own % per player; the
   `pOwn%` column and `Own Diff` leverage signal.
8. `sabersim.com/dfs/draftkings` ($7/7-day trial) — lineup rules builder and contest sim
   controls; how they structure exposure, team stacks, game stacks.
9. `oddsshopper.com/` — Portfolio EV method; how they do custom devigging.
10. `rbsdm.com/stats/` — EPA, Weighted EPA, garbage-time WP filter; the NFL efficiency backbone.

**Tier 3 — calibration and methodology:**
11. `scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html` — Platt, isotonic, temperature scaling,
    reliability diagram code.
12. `arxiv.org/abs/2210.16315` (grouping loss) — full paper; the partitioning algorithm to
    compute the grouping-loss diagnostic.
13. `github.com/aperezlebel/beyond_calibration` — reference implementation; `src/partitioning.py`
    `cluster_evaluate` function.
14. `baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search` — pitch-level data: spin rate, release point,
    movement per pitch.

**Tier 4 — competitive intel:**
15. `rotogrinders.com/` (logged in) — LineupHQ optimizer internals, SimLabs, THE BAT projections.
16. `fantasylabs.com/` — Player Models, Trends, Contest Ownership.
17. `actionnetwork.com/` — how they present edge, +EV, public betting splits.
18. `bettingpros.com/` — consensus picks, expert picks, aggregation method.

**Do NOT scrape:** sportsbook sites for display prices without a license; fantasy sites that
prohibit scraping (check `source-rights-registry.ts` first); anything that would put a real
book's quotes into a paid SaaS without rights.

**What each scrape unlocks** (verbatim): Statcast batters → MLB `underlying` factor
(barrel%, hard-hit%, EV50); Statcast pitchers → pitcher `underlying` (spin, whiff, chase);
Fangraphs → cross-model comparison vs our projections; PropFinder NFL → `matchupSplit`
factor (zone vs man, box counts); PrizePicks/Underdog → `consensus` factor (over/under split);
LineStar Props data → L5/L10 form + Matchup+ Imp in the projections table; LineStar Ownership →
real pOwn% and Own Diff; SaberSim → contest sim and stack rules structure; OddsShopper →
custom devigging method; RBSDM → NFL EPA backbone; grouping-loss paper → the diagnostic that
says whether RES=0 is "no signal" or "collapsed signal".

### 4b. Scrape wave 2 results — the wiring map

Source: `docs/research/scrape-wave-2-results.md` (2026-09-12). Source of the extracts:
founder-pasted extract JSON (`extract-data-2026-09-12 (1).json`): 71 feature inventory items,
567 data columns, 34 verbatim formulas, 12 pricing observations, 4 calibration claims,
39 export/API paths, 17 paywalled features, deep structure keys for RBSDM and NFL/Savant.
"Do not re-scrape these URLs."

**Tier 1 — factor engine inputs (wire these first):**

*MLB Statcast batters → `underlying` factor* (baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_leaderboard +
expected_statistics + sprint_speed). Columns per player (confirmed): EV (avg exit velocity,
MPH); EV50 (avg of hardest 50% of batted balls; for pitchers, softest 50% allowed); LA
(launch angle, degrees); LA SwSp% (launch angle sweet-spot %); Hard Hit % (95 MPH+); Barrels
count, Brls/BBE%, Brls/PA%; Distance (avg feet); xBA, xSLG, xwOBA + Diff columns (actual minus
expected); Sprint Speed (ft/sec, fastest one-second window; best ~2/3 of competitive runs
averaged); Bolts (runs at or above 30 ft/sec); HP to 1B (home to first, seconds).
Formulas (verbatim from Savant): Hit Probability assigned from exit velocity and launch angle
of each batted ball, based on outcomes of comparable historic balls in play; expected season
metrics accumulate expected outcomes of each batted ball with actual strikeouts, walks and HBPs;
Sprint Speed = "feet per second in a player's fastest one-second window" on individual plays,
best ~2/3 averaged for seasonal figure; MLB average competitive sprint speed: 27 ft/sec
(range ~23 poor to ~30 elite). Wiring target: `apps/web/lib/statcast/` (new), mirror nflverse
loader pattern. Factor input: `underlying: { barrelPct, hardHitPct, ev50, xwOBA, sprintSpeed }`.

*MLB Statcast pitchers → pitcher `underlying` factor* (baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search).
Columns per pitch/pitcher (confirmed): Pitch Velocity (MPH), Perceived Velocity (MPH); Spin
Rate (RPM); Vertical/Horizontal Release Point (feet), Release Extension (feet); Arm Angle
(degrees); Plate Horizontal/Vertical (feet); Whiff Rate, Chase% (from metric keys); xBA, xSLG,
xwOBA allowed; Barrel/BBE%, Barrel/PA% allowed; Hard Hit% allowed. Metric keys offered in
search UI: PA, AB, BIP, Hits, 1B/2B/3B/HR, SO, K%, BB, BB%, HBP, Whiffs, Swings, xBA, xOBP,
xSLG, xwOBA, Barrels, BABIP, ISO, Whiff Rate, Run Value, Pitch Velocity, Spin Rate, Exit
Velocity, Launch Angle, Hit Distance, Hard Hit%, Barrel/BBE%, Barrel/PA%.

*PropFinder NFL → `matchupSplit` factor:* /nfl is sign-in gated. Marketing page confirms the
data model: target share, snap counts, coverage matchups, QB adjustments, model spreads and
totals; sportsbooks: DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Caesars, ESPN Bet, Fanatics, PrizePicks,
Underdog; sports: NFL, CFB, MLB, WNBA, NBA, NHL. Wiring target: `apps/web/lib/nfl/coverage-splits.ts`
(new). Factor input: `matchupSplit: { vsMan, vsZone, vsLightBox, vsStackedBox, sampleSize }`.
Blocker: needs founder login credentials for PropFinder, or use nflverse play-by-play which
already has coverage data.

*PrizePicks/Underdog → `consensus` factor:* not in this scrape; PropFinder marketing confirms
both books are in their odds mix. Wiring target: `apps/web/lib/consensus/public-picks.ts` (new).
Factor input: `consensus: { overCount, underCount }`. **Rule: NEVER fabricate. Absent = factor
does not fire.**

**Tier 2 — optimizer and props board parity:**

*LineStar Projections table (full column set confirmed):* Status (label); Chat; Value (X
multiplier, e.g. 3.5X); Salary (USD, e.g. $5,800); Projection (fantasy pts, model); Consensus
(fantasy pts, market); Max Exp% (percent); Cons Diff (fantasy pts, Projection minus Consensus);
Time (game time); Opponent (team); vs Pos (rank, opponent positional rank); Floor (fantasy
pts); Ceiling (fantasy pts); Range (floor-to-ceiling spread); AlertScore (composite alert);
Avg FP (fantasy pts/game); Imp Pts (implied points); Matchup Data (tags); SIC Score
(Sports Injury Calculator); pOwn (projected ownership %); Leverage (score); Safety (score).
Our projections table already had: Sal, Proj, Val, Ceil, L5, M/U, pOwn%, Lev.
**Gap:** Consensus, Cons Diff, Max Exp%, AlertScore, SIC Score, Safety, Imp Pts, vs Pos, Range.

*LineStar Props board (full column set confirmed)* — groups: PLAYER, RECENT FORM, PROJECTION,
MARKET ODDS, EDGE, MATCHUP. Columns: Last 5 / Last 10 / Season (hit-rate %); Projection / Pick
(model projection); Consensus (market); Line (prop threshold); Over / Under (selection +
American odds); Sportsbook (book name); +EV / Edge % (percent); Matchup+ Imp (matchup impact);
Matchup tags (categorical). Our props board already had market + team filters.
**Gap:** L5/L10/Season hit rates, Matchup+ Imp, Consensus column, +EV column.

*Competitor pricing (competitive intel):* LineStar Premium $39.99/mo or $239.99/yr (unlimited
projections, all apps/website, every sport: NFL/MLB/NBA/NHL/PGA/CFB/CBB/WNBA/UFC/NAS/CSGO/LOL/CFL);
PropFinder Monthly $14.99 / Yearly $149.99 (free tier: 1 game/league; sports: MLB, NBA, NFL,
CFB, NHL, WNBA); Props.Cash $19.99/mo or $199.99/yr (NBA Pass $99.99/yr); Outlier Premium
$19.99/mo, Premium+ $29.99/mo, Pro $79.99/mo; PlayerProps.ai 6-mo VIP $295; PickFinder
Premium $149.99/yr, Pro $299.99/yr; SaberSim $7 for 7 days trial.

**Tier 3 — methodology and calibration:**

*Fangraphs projection models (confirmed list):* pre-season: ZiPS, ZiPS DC, Steamer, Depth
Charts, ATC, THE BAT, THE BAT X, OOPSY. In-season: updated, RoS, 600 PA/200 IP, three-year
ZiPS, On-Pace. Pagination: 4186 default results; ATC bat 631; ATC pit 855. Model authors
credited: Dan Szymborski (ZiPS), steamerprojections.com, FanGraphs staff, Ariel Cohen (ATC),
Derek Carty (THE BAT), Jordan Rosenblum, Eno Sarris. **No equations published. Weights not
disclosed. This is competitive intel only.**

*RBSDM (NFL efficiency backbone):* JSON API keys observed: min_season, max_season,
season_week_bounds, teams, generated_at. Tabs: Team Tiers, Offense, Defense, Quarterbacks,
Neutral Pass Freq, Pass Over Expected, Fourth Downs, Luck, Series Success. Formulas: Pass Over
Expected Difference = Actual − Expected; Series Conv % = TD / 1st Down / FG / Punt / TO outcome
percentages. Filters: season min/max (2020+), regular week min/max, postseason
(None/WC/DIV/CONF/SB), downs 1-4, quarters 1-4/OT, garbage-time WP filter, exclude-turnovers.

*NFL/Savant (JSON API):* API response keys: week, metrics, category, unit, rows, columns. Row
keys: id, name, team, pos, v, qualified, values. Value keys: epa, comp, att, comp_pct, yds, ya,
td, int, sacks, cpoe, pressure_pct, succ, adot. Formulas (verbatim): EPA/play = how much a QB
raises or lowers his team's scoring expectation on each pass play; Rushing YOE = actual yards
minus what an average back would gain from the same situation; Pressure % = share of opposing
dropbacks where this defender recorded a sack or QB hit. Provenance: play-by-play via nflverse;
charting data FTN Data + NFL Next Gen Stats via nflverse (CC-BY-SA 4.0).

*Next Gen Stats columns* (kept with attribution per the no-dedupe directive; also inventoried in
the sweep's ngs-digest): Receiving: CUSH, SEP, TAY, TAY%, REC, TAR, CTCH%, YDS, TD, YAC/R,
xYAC/R, +/-. Rushing: EFF, 8+D%, TLOS, ATT, YDS, RYOE, AVG, RYOE/Att, ROE%, TD.

*Basketball-Reference advanced* (data-stat keys): ranker, name_display, age, team_name_abbr,
pos, games, games_started, mp, per, ts_pct, fg3a_per_fga_pct, fta_per_fga_pct, orb_pct, drb_pct,
trb_pct, ast_pct, stl_pct, blk_pct, tov_pct, usg_pct, ows, dws, ws, ws_per_48, obpm, dbpm, bpm,
vorp, awards. VORP tooltip: "Multiply by 2.70 to convert to wins over replacement".

**Tier 4 — competitive intel and alerts:**

*Alert/notification patterns observed:* LineStar — AlertScore + alert icons (Expected Starter,
Good Vegas Odds, opponent ranks, favored/away splits, recent-form); SaberSim — real-time alerts
for breaking news and surprise scratches; Outlier — save filters, notify when opportunities
fit; PickFinder — Discord notifications for new/updated lines; PlayerProps.ai — premium
community line movement alerts.

*Paywall patterns:* Stathead — subscription (first month free promo); LineStar full projections —
Premium; LineStar PropsAI full data — Premium (limited free set); PropFinder NFL dashboard —
Auth (sign-in); RotoGrinders premium tools — Premium Only badge; Data Export — Members Only;
Historical Projections — Members Exclusive; Percentile Outcomes wOBA — Members mode; Cleaning
the Glass — Subscribe (error page in capture); SaberSim optimizer — Paid ($7/7 days); Outlier
advanced — Premium/Premium+/Pro; PlayerProps.ai premium — subscription tiers; PickFinder
EV+/arb/middles — Pro annual; Props.Cash full analytics — paid plans.

*RotoGrinders prop evaluation example (verbatim):* "The line of 4.5 compares favorably based on
our MLB simulations. The prop projects to hit 72.81% of the time based on the assumptions, and
that represents an 11.27% edge."

*Calibration claims observed:* PickFinder community testimonial: 65% accuracy (member for 2
months, under a month of winnings) — testimonial only, not a measured claim. LineStar:
"independently verified as one of the best in the industry" — no sample size or metric
published. Sprint speed: 27 ft/sec MLB average, 23-30 competitive range.

**Wiring priority (updated):** 1. Statcast batters loader → MLB `underlying` (no blocker, public
CSV); 2. Statcast pitchers loader → pitcher `underlying` (none); 3. RBSDM EPA backbone (none,
JSON API); 4. NFL/Savant JSON → pressure%, EPA, RYOE (none); 5. NGS receiving/rushing →
air yards, separation, RYOE (none, public tables); 6. PropFinder NFL cheatsheets →
`matchupSplit` (sign-in required); 7. PrizePicks/Underdog consensus → `consensus` (not in this
scrape); 8. LineStar Props L5/L10 data → hit-rate columns (premium); 9. LineStar Ownership →
real pOwn% and Own Diff (premium); 10. Fangraphs ATC/THE BAT → cross-model comparison (none
for structure, premium for data).

**Already wired (from wave 1 + ASTRA):** projections table Sal, Proj, Val, Ceil, L5, M/U,
pOwn%, Lev; props board market + team filters; CSV export (DK Classic); max exposure slider
(10-100%); factor engine skeleton: depth chart, injury, matchup split, underlying, consensus,
rest.

**This scrape added (column definitions + formulas, ready to wire):** Statcast EV50, Hard Hit%,
Barrels, LA SwSp%, xBA/xSLG/xwOBA, Sprint Speed, Bolts; pitcher spin rate, perceived velo,
release point, arm angle, whiff%, chase%; LineStar gap columns (Consensus, Cons Diff,
AlertScore, SIC Score, Safety, Imp Pts, vs Pos, Range); props gap columns (L5/L10/Season hit
rates, Matchup+ Imp, +EV); RBSDM EPA/play, Pass Over Expected, Series Success, garbage-time
WP filter; NFL/Savant pressure%, EPA/play, RYOE, CPOE, ADOT; NGS CUSH, SEP, TAY%, YAC/R,
xYAC/R, EFF, 8+D%, RYOE/Att.

**Still blocked:** PropFinder NFL board (sign-in); LineStar Props/Ownership data (premium);
PrizePicks/Underdog public pick % (not scraped); SaberSim contest sim internals (paid).

### 4c. Competitor scrape reference (wave-1 prompt + formulas)

Source: `docs/research/competitor-scrape-2026-09-12.md`. Scraped sites: LineStar, PropFinder,
RotoGrinders, RotoWire, SaberSim, OddsShopper, Statcast, Fangraphs, Baseball-Reference,
Pro-Football-Reference, Basketball-Reference, Hockey-Reference, NFL Savant, RBSDM, The Odds
API, Polymarket, DraftKings, scikit-learn, arXiv (grouping loss), nflverse.

**LineStar Props table columns (the target):** position/team; Recent Form (Last 5, Last 10,
Season, Last LG); Projection (their number + confidence read); Market (odds, prop line/type);
Edge (+EV, Edge %); Matchup (Matchup+ Imp, Matchup); Pick/consensus (Over/Under split);
Over/Under; Chat (community). **Our projections table already ships:** Sal, Proj, Val, Ceil,
pOwn%, Lev. **Missing vs LineStar:** Recent Form windows, Matchup impact, Over/Under consensus.

**Statcast columns (underlying metrics):** EV50 — avg of hardest 50% of batted balls (batter) /
softest 50% allowed (pitcher); Hard Hit 95 MPH+ (%), Hard Hit (%); Barrels #, Brls/BBE (%),
Brls/PA (%); LA SwSp% (Launch Angle Sweet-Spot %); Exit Velocity Max/Avg (MPH); Distance
Max/Avg (ft); qualifiers: 2.1 PA/team game (batters), 1.25 PA/team game (pitchers).

**PropFinder NFL/CFB columns:** target share, snap counts, coverage matchups, weekly usage
trends; TD/rushing/redzone/line/coverage matchup cheatsheets; hit rates, opponent matchup
ranks; QB rankings, win totals, home-field advantage, weather; model spreads, totals,
projections, win probability.

**Formulas captured (verbatim):** Platt scaling: `p(y=1|f) = 1/(1+exp(Af+B))`, A and B fitted
by MLE. Isotonic objective: `sum (y_i - f^i)^2` s.t. `f^i >= f^j whenever f_i >= f_j`.
Temperature scaling: `softmax(z/T)`. EV50: average of hardest 50% (batter) / softest 50%
allowed (pitcher). Grouping loss (arXiv 2210.16315): "given the calibration loss, the missing
piece to characterize individual errors is the grouping loss". PickFinder: "every price against
a devigged fair line, ranked by edge". SaberSim: "simulates every game thousands of times,
play-by-play".

**Scoring / ranking logic captured:** RotoWire — "most projected fantasy points for each
roster spot while balancing salary-cap restrictions and stacking". SaberSim — "high-upside
lineups and optimize for ROI"; controls player exposures, team stacks, game stacks. PickFinder —
"EV+ prices against a devigged fair line, ranked by edge". RBSDM — EPA and Weighted EPA views,
garbage-time win-probability filter.

**What to scrape next (wave-1 verdict):** (1) LineStar Props deep page (logged in) — actual
Recent Form numbers, Matchup+ Imp values, confidence formula; (2) PropFinder NFL cheatsheets
(logged in) — TD/rushing/redzone/line/coverage data; (3) SaberSim optimizer (trial) — lineup
rules builder, contest sim controls; (4) OddsShopper Portfolio EV — custom devigging method;
(5) Fangraphs projections (ATC, THE BAT, Steamer, ZiPS) — model families and weights; (6)
nflverse Next Gen Stats — sprint speed, time to throw, separation (already in source registry;
needs the license check); (7) PrizePicks/Underdog public pick % — the consensus over/under
split for the 5,000-over/3,700-under factor.

### 4d. Record-accuracy fixes (2026-09-12 adversarial audit outcomes)

Source: `docs/research/session-handoff-2026-09-12.md`. From the ASTRA redesign session (agent
worked autonomously, 20+ PRs merged to main as PRs #769-#791, then 20+ more on founder
feedback; branch `claude/astra-redesign-2026-09-14`, fully merged, 0 ahead of main).

**Production live truth surface at handoff (2026-09-12T02:00Z):** calibrationEligibility GREEN,
streak 93; canExposePerformanceStats true; calibrationPublished true; revenueLadder PROVEN;
settlement HEALTHY (0 of 2806 overdue); canonicalSettled 2300; MODEL_VERSION v5.2.7 (untouched);
floors n 100 / Brier 0.22 / ECE 0.05 (untouched). **The only ESTABLISHED blocker: CLV
beat-close 23.0% vs 52.4% required** — a model problem, not a gate problem. The selective path
(δ=0.1, rank on marketFairProb) is ON; historical projection of that filtered set passes
floors (Brier 0.150, RES 0.041).

**Record-accuracy fixes shipped (the big ones):**
- PUSH was structurally unreachable for spreads/totals. Published and graded the POSTED book
  line (`published-line.ts`). Scoring math still reads the raw mean. MODEL_VERSION unchanged.
  Ties resolve against us.
- Published bet terms frozen write-once at creation (selection/line/reasoning/reasoningShort).
  The card can no longer show -4.5 while we grade -3.0.
- Calibration bucket win rates excluded pushes (were averaging push as half a win, flattering
  sub-50% buckets). Correlation WIN_RATE excluded pushes (were counting every push as a loss).
- /api/performance floor counts decided picks only (was counting pushes).

**Also shipped:** founder picks system (`lib/founder-picks/`, modelVersion=founder-v1,
isBootstrap=false; factor engine: depth chart, teammate OUT, OL OUT, injury, matchup split,
underlying metric, consensus, rest/B2B; 15 unit tests); GSE Score + GSE Index
(`lib/fantasy/gse-score.ts` — LIVE reads processGrade from nflverse, SAMPLE is pool
percentile; 8 unit tests); calibration skill metrics (BSS, NLL, Murphy, null-band ECE —
additive, no floors); per-market gate; LineStar/PropFinder parity (projections table,
sortable, CSV export DK Classic, max exposure slider 10-100%, props board market+team
filters); Lens Switcher fix (FAN=plain English, BETTOR=Edge Index + bet meaning,
CREATOR=story angle, ANALYST=all numbers); jargon strip (JSON buttons gone, engine titles
plain); copy replacements: "cleared the gate" → "we're on this", "held" → "passed",
"market depth below publish threshold" → "not enough sportsbooks are pricing this game yet".

**Open at handoff (founder env actions, agents cannot flip):** `EVENT_ODDS_INGEST_ENABLED=true`
(prop-line ingest); `ADMIN_EMAILS` allow-list (code allow-list `CODE_OWNER_ALLOWLIST` in

`INTERNAL_LLM_BASE_URL=https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1` + the Vercel AI Gateway key (was sent

`postcss` (vulnerability gone; waiver list needs entries removed; frozen by law — founder
action); 25/26 other guardrails pass.

**The laws (do not violate):** (1) NEVER `git push` to main directly — PRs only; (2) NEVER
modify: schema.prisma, migrations, .github/workflows, scripts/guardrails, .claude, any .env*,
package-lock.json, .gitignore, .githooks, ai-control-plane; (3) NEVER flip a gate or env flag —
founder-only; (4) NEVER write a claim you did not observe; (5) NEVER mark DONE without the DoD
commands actually passing; (6) NEVER `git commit --no-verify`; (7) NEVER install a package, run
a migration, or touch a database; (8) NEVER fabricate product data; (9) NEVER weaken a guard to

title: NFL-RevEng-KB | 5. Evidence-source strategy (2026-05-21) [Pre-September-17 Research Digest — NFL Analytics Reverse-Engineering Knowledge Base]
body:
## 5. Evidence-source strategy (2026-05-21)

Source: `docs/research/evidence-source-strategy-2026-05-21.md`. Purpose: decide what data sources
can safely power the next Galaxy Sports Edge intelligence layer without breaking the evidence rules.

**Architecture decision:** do not add player/ref/venue/pace factors directly to confidence yet.
Add them to the Evidence Readiness Matrix first: (1) SourceSnapshot proves a provider response
existed; (2) normalization produces an EvidenceRecord / GameSignal; (3) the Evidence Readiness
Matrix decides whether each factor is ACTIVE, SHADOW_READY, SHADOW_COLLECTING, BLOCKED, or ABSENT;
(4) scoring reads only ACTIVE factors explicitly allowed to contribute; (5) true EV remains
blocked until independent fair probability is source-backed and separately promoted.

**Provider surfaces reviewed:** The Odds API (live odds endpoint, core markets, paid quota,
historical odds/player-prop/business-tier notes, explicit API-key/header behavior —
https://theoddsapi.com/); Sportradar Sports Data API (broad official/commercial coverage —
https://docs.sportradar.com/sports-data-api); SportsDataIO (sports data, injuries, lineups/depth
charts, standings, betting data, historical odds, ID mapping, widgets, league-specific APIs —
https://sportsdata.io/); Open-Meteo (forecast and archived forecast APIs with coordinates,
hourly variables, multiple weather models, historical forecast runs —
https://open-meteo.com/en/docs).

**Provider fit:**
- **Market odds** — start here; paid key already present; deploy-readiness confirmed 20,000
  requests remaining. Use: live odds; scores/settlement; historical odds only if the current
  plan includes it. Risks: quota exhaustion inside 2 weeks; stale line movement if
  opening/current prices are not preserved; false "edge" if market-derived fair price gets
  mistaken for independent probability.
- **Player availability** — use only official/licensed injury, lineup, depth-chart feeds
  (SportsDataIO or Sportradar). Risks: late scratches; inconsistent team phrasing
  ("questionable" vs "game-time decision"); player ID mapping drift across providers. Matrix
  posture: SHADOW_ONLY until enough settled outcome history proves incremental calibration value.
- **Officials / referees** — use only licensed assignment and historical same-sport trend feeds
  (Sportradar if coverage includes official assignment; league official sources if terms permit).
  Risks: small samples; playoff/prime-time assignment bias; crew composition changes. Matrix
  posture: SHADOW_ONLY with high min sample size.
- **Venue environment** — venue coordinates + game-time weather/roof/surface state (Open-Meteo
  for weather where outdoor conditions matter; licensed schedule/venue metadata for
  roof/surface/park state). Risks: roof decisions; wind shifts near first pitch/kickoff;
  incorrectly geocoded stadiums. Matrix posture: weather can be useful quickly, but it must age
  out aggressively.
- **Pace / team rates** — use league/team stat feeds, not LLM summaries (SportsDataIO,
  Sportradar, or league APIs where legally allowed). Risks: early-season samples; injuries
  changing tempo; garbage-time distortion. Matrix posture: SHADOW_ONLY until bucket-level Brier
  improvement is measured.

**What changed in code:** `packages/prediction-engine/src/evidence-readiness-matrix.ts` plus
tests — executable definitions for market board, line movement, rest state, schedule density,
pace profile, division context, player availability, officials, venue environment, venue
history, milestone context, independent fair probability, true EV. Each factor carries: source
categories, minimum trust, minimum sample size, freshness window, scoring eligibility,
activation requirement, failure horizon, likely failure mode. "This is intentionally boring
infrastructure. It is the layer that lets the product become aggressive later without becoming
sloppy now."

title: NFL-RevEng-KB | 6. Brand and commentary voice rules a coding agent generating copy must follow [Pre-September-17 Research Digest — NFL Analytics Reverse-Engineering Knowledge Base]
body:
## 6. Brand and commentary voice rules a coding agent generating copy must follow

### 6a. Galaxy Sports Edge NFL commentary brand research (2026-09-10)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-10-galaxy-commentary-brand/final-report.md`. Every finding carries
an exact source URL; paper policy separated from observed practice; unconfirmable items marked
UNVERIFIED. Not legal advice. The account's stated posture: transformative, commentary-led,
seconds-long telestrated edits — never standalone rips or compilations.

**TOPIC 1 — how 3–5 top NFL film-breakdown creators actually operate:**
- **NFL Access Pass (2023):** opened to a "select group" of creators, granting "officially
  approved footage" with monetization allowed on YouTube; NFL executive Ian Trombetta noted
  "tight parameters" on what footage is approved (digiday.com;
  sportsbusinessjournal.com 2023-09-14). As of 2025-01-30, the Access Pass roster included
  **Brett Kollmann**, with **J.T. O'Sullivan** and **Kurt Benkert** named for Access Pass for
  Legends; Year 1 covered 24 creators and 200M+ views (sportsvideo.org 2025-01-30). Legends
  lets former players use official highlights, Super Bowl, NFL Draft, other footage while
  retaining a share of ad revenue (news.bloomberglaw.com). **Key conclusion:** Kollmann's,
  O'Sullivan's, and Benkert's current footage is at least partly **expressly licensed** — their
  survival is not proof an unaffiliated account faces the same enforcement. Copy their
  editorial structure (segmenting, telestration, slow-mo loops), not their apparent footage
  tolerance. Track and apply for Access Pass when eligible.
- **Tim Jenkins / All Things QB (Front Office Sports, 2026):** long-form 30+ min videos;
  creators "loop through the same play at different angles and use a telestrator"; Jenkins
  posts **two public videos weekly and two members-only clips**; a 30-minute episode takes
  ~**2–3 hours**, mostly identifying plays; toolchain **Hudl for telestration**, **OBS Studio**
  to record his screen, light editing after; the report expressly notes creators outside
  Access Pass are "taking a risk". Exploit: standardize repeatable screen-record → telestrate →
  loop-angles workflow (free: OBS + any telestration tool; Hudl is the paid reference). Keep a
  footage-light public version; paywalling does not cure copyright risk. UNVERIFIED: whether
  Jenkins is licensed, his exact footage source, per-play seconds, claims history.
- **All-22 sourcing:** historically Game Pass offered broadcasts and All-22; analysts described
  accessing international Game Pass, QuickTime screen-recording All-22, sharing files privately
  (Defector) — observed practice, not permission. Exploit: use legitimate viewing access
  (e.g., NFL+ NFL Pro's All-22 offering) to *study* plays, then rebuild the teaching point as
  original diagrams whenever footage rights are uncertain.
- **Enforcement history:** in 2007 the NFL objected to **20 seconds of game footage** in law
  professor Wendy Seltzer's copyright-warning video; NFL counsel: "We do not see how the use
  of such game content has any educational purposes or character" (sportsbusinessjournal.com;
  deadspin.com). A legal article reports the NFL requested removal of **more than 3,000
  YouTube clips in 2006** (gould.usc.edu). Exploit: **no safe "under X seconds" rule exists** —
  make every second necessary to active criticism (pause, annotate, narrate); avoid
  uninterrupted highlight value.
- **Closest thing to a charter:** CMSI Code of Best Practices in Fair Use for Online Video,
  Principle TWO — "Using copyrighted material for illustration or example": fair when important
  to the larger purpose but subordinate to it; fair when not presented for its original purpose
  but harnessed for a new one; illustrative quotations "should be drawn from a range of
  different sources" where possible and "no longer than is necessary to achieve the intended
  effect"; proper attribution reduces complaint likelihood (cmsimpact.org). Exploit: this is
  the argumentative frame for telestrated breakdowns — footage subordinate to analysis, used
  for teaching, kept to minimum, attributed.
- **Reconstruction/animation alternatives:** Kurt Benkert produces Madden-based teaching content
  (Front Office Sports); Samuel Gold published film-room articles with named concepts and
  original play diagrams (fieldgulls.com 2016). Exploit: when footage rights are uncertain,
  rebuild teaching points with Madden captures or original overhead dot/route diagrams.
  UNVERIFIED: whether any named creator uses animated dots/diagrams as a *systematic* footage
  substitute — build that ourselves.

**TOPIC 2 — beat reporters/outlets: reuse permissions; facts, quotations, X reposts:**
- **Facts and game results are not protected expression.** *NBA v. Motorola*, 105 F.3d 841
  (2d Cir. 1997): "Motorola and STATS did not infringe NBA's copyright because they reproduced
  only facts from the broadcasts, not the expression or description of the game that
  constitutes the broadcast"; "No author may copyright facts or ideas." Exploit: independently
  write posts from scores, down/distance, formations, play outcomes, statistics. Do not copy a
  reporter's phrasing, graphic design, database, or footage just because the underlying facts
  are free.
- **PFF — unusually explicit creator permission (updated 2026-09-04):** pff.com/terms §1.9
  permits sharing, quoting, or screenshotting **individual PFF grades, statistics, or excerpts
  of free articles** on personal, noncommercial social accounts with attribution/linking and
  without bulk substitution. §1.10 expressly permits monetized creator content (videos,
  streams, podcasts, newsletters, articles, social content) to "reference, quote, or display
  individual items of Free Content," provided each item credits PFF, links where possible, is
  not bulk/database-like, does not substitute for PFF, and is not presented as endorsed by
  PFF. Paid content, API data, and AI output excluded. Exploit: one public PFF grade/stat per
  post, labeled "Source: PFF," with a link and original analysis on top. Never publish paid-only
  tables or bulk rankings.
- **The Athletic (NYT) — no sharing clause, no CC license:** terms grant only "a limited,
  revocable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to access and use the Services";
  sharing only "with our prior written permission... or as expressly permitted by these
  Terms." The NYT fair-use policy is in fact a contact page for *requesting licenses* —
  operative posture is request-permission-first. Exploit: link to Athletic articles; restate
  facts independently; use short quotation only under a separate fair-use analysis. Never rely
  on "credit" as permission.
- **ESPN/Disney — restrictive terms:** personal, noncommercial consumer license only; "no
  right to reproduce, distribute, communicate to the public, make available to the public, or
  transform any Disney Product"; no "use the Disney Products for any commercial or
  business-related use or build a business utilizing the Disney Products," except where
  applicable law overrides (disneytermsofuse.com). Exploit: link out; use platform-native
  sanctioned sharing; extract independently restated facts and short quotations under
  fair-use analysis only.
- **X reposts and quote posts:** X's 2026 terms — users retain ownership but grant X a
  worldwide license authorizing X to make content available and "let others do the same,"
  including "syndication, broadcast, distribution, repost, promotion or publication," subject
  to X's terms — this licenses **X and its sublicensees**, not a user downloading and
  re-uploading someone else's video. Quote post mechanics (2026 guide): click repost icon →
  select Quote → "Write your take above the embedded original" → post; "Quote posting wraps
  the original in your own commentary... The commentary sits above the embedded post, so your
  text gets read first." Exploit: quote-post official @NFL and team posts — the original
  stays embedded and attributed, commentary lives in *our* post. Never download and re-upload
  their video files. UNVERIFIED: no current official X help-center article documenting
  repost/quote was locatable; the ToS-based reading is the strongest available basis.
- **Quotations — no bright-line rule:** the U.S. Copyright Office: "there is no formula to
  ensure that a predetermined percentage or amount of a work — or specific number of words,
  lines, pages, copies — may be used without permission." Even a small amount can weigh
  against fair use if it is the "heart" of the work (*Harper & Row v. Nation*). Exploit:
  quote only what is needed to identify and critique the source; surrounding original
  analysis should dominate. Never promise "1–2 sentences" is automatically fair.
- **NFL press releases vs. NFL footage — separate the two:** NFL.com/news press-release content
  (signings, rule changes, statements) is routinely and freely quotable/redistributable as news
  with attribution. That practice concerns **text**, not game footage; nothing in it waives
  rights over broadcast/game video. Exploit: quote press releases and official statements
  freely with attribution; treat footage under an entirely separate analysis.

**TOPIC 3 — underused zero-cost opportunities:**
- **YouTube embeds** expressly licensed through the Service: "You may also show YouTube videos
  through the embeddable YouTube player"; uploaders grant use "only as enabled by a feature of
  the Service (such as video playback or embeds)" — does not authorize use independent of
  YouTube. Exploit: embed official NFL YouTube videos on a website (player intact); does NOT
  authorize cropping footage into an independently uploaded X video.
- **Getty Embed** — real zero-dollar option with hard limits: 70M+ photos on a **noncommercial**
  website or blog — not for selling, raising money, promotion, or endorsement; editorial/
  newsworthy/public-interest purposes only; no advertising, promotions, merchandising, implied
  endorsement, unlawful use, or display outside the Embedded Viewer; Getty may remove content or
  monetize the viewer. Exploit: use Getty's own embed player in a non-promotional editorial
  site article. Do not download Getty images or place them in X graphics, thumbnails, ads, or
  sales pages.
- **GIPHY embed vs. reuse:** support page instructs select "Embed," choose iframe or HTML5,
  paste code, publish; GIPHY terms: "we grant each user of the Services a worldwide,
  non-exclusive, non-sublicensable and non-transferable license to use Content solely for
  purposes of using the Services. Use, reproduction, modification, distribution or storage of
  any Content for other than purposes of using the Services is expressly prohibited without
  prior written permission." Historical context: a 2016 NFL–GIPHY "test agreement" made Giphy
  "the source of high quality and authentic NFL GIFs of ancillary game and historical/iconic
  content" — **not gameplay GIFs** (techcrunch.com 2016-12-02). Exploit: use GIPHY's hosted
  embed/player where an official NFL GIF exists; never download and re-upload GIFs to X.
  UNVERIFIED: whether an official @NFL GIPHY channel is currently active with current uploads.
- **Wikimedia Commons** — genuinely free NFL game photos (not video): Commons hosts NFL game
  photos (e.g., All-Pro Reels transfers from Flickr via #flickr2commons, 2021 Washington at
  Falcons). Exploit: use as thumbnails, post headers, site imagery with required attribution.
  **Caution (UNVERIFIED per file):** confirm each file's license field before commercial/
  monetized use.
- **AP Images** — priced, not free; public a la carte accounts exist. A 2014 report: editorial
  web use for two years of one photo ~$95 (poynter.org). Price UNVERIFIED as current. USA Today
  Sports Images similarly licensed stock; no zero-dollar editorial embed tier located.
- **No current official fan clip-sharing tool found** (UNVERIFIED — feature not located): no
  current NFL app / NFL+ "make your own clip and share to social" feature in public
  documentation. What exists: NFL+ "NFL Pro" offers **All-22 Coaches Film for every game
  dating back to the 2022 season**, playlist saving/sharing — viewing/playlist features, not
  re-upload rights (sportsvideo.org 2024-08-21). The 2008-era NFL.com "Replay Re-Cutter" is
  discontinued. Notably even **teams** historically could not create their own gameplay GIFs and
  had to rely on the NFL's social team (large violation fines) — the league does not take a
  permissive posture on third-party gameplay-video redistribution.
- **The pre-1964 public-domain avenue exists but is item-specific:** Library of Congress —
  "Published works registered for copyright in the U.S. through Dec. 31, 1963 are now in the
  public domain **unless the copyright was renewed**" — and the only way to determine renewal
  status is a copyright search. Exploit: genuine path for historical material, but requires a
  **per-item renewal search** — archive.org hosting alone proves nothing. Default assumption
  for any NFL footage: still under copyright unless an item-specific search says otherwise.
- **Public-domain NFL footage is not established (general rule):** Internet Archive hosts
  batches labeled 1945/1956/1959 NFL seasons, but the preservation project itself says some
  material cannot be uploaded due to copyright constraints; the NFL has affirmatively claimed
  copyright over historic footage such as Super Bowl I. Exploit: do not use "old NFL footage"
  merely because it is old or archived; use only items with an item-specific rights statement,
  renewal search, or written permission; build original diagrams from historical facts instead.

**Appendix items deliberately excluded:** a PDF at an assets.website-files.com URL titled "The
Athletic Cos. Website Terms of Use" was not confirmed to be the NYT-owned Athletic (the real
NYT terms were used instead); forum/Reddit speculation about creator copyright treatment was
treated as non-evidence; disclaimers ("all rights go to...," "no infringement intended") grant
no permission — noted, not used.

### 6b. Pundit-signal legal research framework (2026-06-13)

Source: `docs/research/pundit-signal-legal-research-prompt.md`. A deep-research prompt engineered
for a reasoning model, designed to map every LAWFUL path to "use the analytical substance of
sports-pundit commentary as a graded input signal in a commercial prediction product, without
infringing copyright or breaching contract" — and to stress-test every avenue against actual
case law, not rationalize a predetermined answer. Context: SiriusXM Fantasy Sports Radio shows
(e.g. "Elite Sports with Jeff Mans"); constraints already known: SiriusXM's Customer Agreement
(§9 / "AI Matters") restricts content to personal, non-commercial use, prohibits using their
content to create, train, or improve any AI service, prohibits scraping/recording/automated
extraction; content is account-gated (paid subscription) and copyrighted broadcast expression.
Many pundits also publish public podcasts (e.g. "One MANS Opinion" on Podbean/Apple) under
different terms.

**Research questions the framework requires answered with citations:** (A) copyright line —
facts vs expression (Feist v. Rural Telephone 1991; 17 U.S.C. §102(b)); is a pundit's
prediction/opinion protectable or unprotectable once expressed; human-authored original
summaries/paraphrases vs machine paraphrase of a fixed transcript (derivative work).
(B) Fair use — all four factors of 17 U.S.C. §107 applied to (a) human-authored attributed
paraphrase log used commercially, (b) storing verbatim transcript for internal AI training;
**the key adverse case: Fox News Network v. TVEyes (2d Cir. 2018)** — search/transcription vs
clipping holdings; **the key AI-training cases: Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence
(D. Del. 2025 — fair use REJECTED for AI training on Westlaw headnotes)** and pending
NYT v. OpenAI, Authors Guild v. OpenAI; contrast with the fair-use winners **Authors Guild v.
Google (2d Cir. 2015)** and **A.V. ex rel. Vanderhye v. iParadigms (Turnitin)** — which side of
the line does "ingest pundit transcripts to improve a commercial prediction model" fall on?
(C) Contract & access — ToS enforceability independent of copyright (can contract bar a use
copyright would permit?); CFAA post-**Van Buren v. United States (2021)** and **hiQ v.
LinkedIn**; is there any "data laundering" doctrine (hypothesis to test: the breach attaches
at the moment of prohibited *use*, regardless of output form). (D) Hot-news misappropriation
(INS v. AP; NBA v. Motorola, 2d Cir. 1997) — could time-sensitive pundit picks be protected,
and does it change near-real-time ingestion? (E) The licensing path (most likely real "yes") —
who owns SiriusXM original programming rights (network, production company, host); media-
monitoring license structures/pricing for small companies; licensed intermediaries/vendors
already relicensing sports-media commentary; content-partnership/affiliate structures with
pundits directly. (F) The public-feed path — podcast platform terms (Podbean/Apple/YouTube)
for automated transcription and derived analytics for commercial use; Creative-Commons or
openly-licensed sports-commentary sources. (G) Precedent in the wild — how consensus-pick
aggregators and tout-grading sites source data lawfully (license, public data, user-submitted,
first-party); open-source rights-respecting ingestion patterns (provenance tracking, license
gating, transcript-rights metadata).

**Required output format:** executive verdict (2–3 viable lawful paths ranked by viability ×
cost × effort; dead paths with one-line reason + controlling authority); path-by-path analysis
(legal basis with citations, concrete steps, cost/effort, residual risk, what to confirm with
retained counsel); the "no" list (each dead path, the controlling case/clause, why a technical
workaround does or does not change the outcome); citations appendix (every case, statute, ToS
clause, vendor, source with a working link and one-line relevance note); counsel brief (1-page
summary the founder can hand to an IP attorney).

**Rules for the research model:** cite or don't claim — every legal proposition gets primary-
source support; distinguish copyright from contract from CFAA at every step — they fail
independently; be current (2023–2026 AI-training fair-use law); if a path requires a license,
say so plainly rather than implying a free workaround exists; flag uncertainty honestly; mark
anything unsettled. This is not legal advice; every claim carries a citation or nothing.

### 6c. Edge Sheet design brief + copy rules (2026-09-17)

Source: `docs/research/2026-09-17/edge-sheet/DESIGN_BRIEF.md` (Worker B deliverable, v1.0).
A single 1080x1350 portrait PNG, one per NFL game, rendered in Python matplotlib; phone-first
(X, TikTok, Instagram). v1 failed as "a text document wearing a dark theme" — v2 rule:
**no paragraph longer than one line anywhere on the sheet; every insight is drawn ON a chart
or it does not ship.**

**FIELD brand system (strict tokens):** Ground `#08090C` (page); Panel `#12141A` (chart cards);
Bone `#EDE8E0` (primary text, BUF identity in charts); Fog `#C4BFB6` (secondary text);
Mist `#8A857C` (muted labels, league-average lines, footnotes); Signal `#FF4D2E` (accent ONLY —
DET identity in charts, the single loudest takeaway per sheet, the fair-line delta); Fog-gray
`#262A33` (the other 30 teams in league-context plots — de-emphasized, not invisible); Hairline
`#1E2128` (panel borders, dividers). No gradients, no glow, no drop shadows, no neon, no
rounded-chart-junk. Clean, sharp, editorial. Two team colors max on any chart. No gradients
/ glow / drop shadows / neon / rounded junk — flat.

**Public copy rules (non-negotiable):** no em dashes; no "sports intelligence" phrasing; human
voice; no hashtag walls; team names in FULL CAPS when large (BILLS / LIONS); `BUF`/`DET`
abbreviations only inside chart legends and data labels. No AI-voice adjectives ("delve,"
"landscape," "tapestry," "in the world of"). Short sentences.

**The 8 charts (each answers one question; if a builder cannot state the question, the chart
is cut):** (1) 32-team efficiency map — hero visual, scatterplot X=offensive EPA/play
Y=defensive EPA/play (up=better defense), 30 teams as fog-gray dots, BUF Bone, DET Signal,
dashed mist crosshairs at league average, direct-label ONLY BUF and DET with team + rank
(e.g. `BUF off #4 / def #9`), one takeaway callout max 12 words with leader line;
(2) 10-metric percentile faceoff — horizontal bar rows, one metric per row, 0–100 percentile
track, BUF/DET markers with value printed bold, league median at 50; rows: Off EPA/play,
Dropback EPA, Rush EPA, Success rate, Explosive play rate, Def EPA/play, Def dropback EPA,
Def rush EPA, Points/drive, Turnover luck; sort rows by combined signal (widest split at
top), not alphabetically; (3) EPA distribution curves — per-play EPA KDE curves (gaussian_kde,
bw ~0.25; fallback: fine histogram + Gaussian smoothing), BUF Bone, DET Signal, league average
dashed mist, X clipped −2 to +2, right-tail mass annotated ("explosive-play share"); (4) unit
vs unit 2x2 grid — pass off vs pass def, rush off vs rush def for both teams, cell background
tinted by winner at alpha 0.10, one arrow or edge per cell toward winner, 5-word verdict on
the biggest EPA-gap cell only; (5) form lines — 4-week rolling offensive EPA/play across 2025
Weeks 1–18, then gap marker, then Week 1 2026 single-game hollow dot ("1-game sample"
footnote); (6) luck ledger — grouped diverging bars, actual vs expected INTs thrown/fumbles
lost/INTs taken, plus a single net-luck strip in approximate points (Signal if team was lucky —
expect regression against them); (7) drive anatomy — second 32-team dot plot, X=points per
drive, Y=giveaway or 3-and-out rate (up=better), smaller than hero; (8) situational edges —
four small multiples: early-down EPA, late-down EPA, red-zone EPA, EPA/dropback under pressure;
identical 0–100 scales on all four (Tufte's rule: comparable panels share axes or the
comparison is a lie).

**League-context treatment (the house style):** every number appears with its league rank,
percentile, or average line — **no orphan numbers; a naked `+0.13` means nothing on a phone.**
30 non-game teams as one gray cloud (never labeled). BUF marker larger with Bone ring, DET
Signal. Direct labeling always beats legends (no legend except possibly the bar field's
BUF/DET key — prefer labeling the markers directly). Max 2 annotated takeaways per chart, 1
preferred, 5–12 words each, sentence case, no em dash, leader lines are hairlines (never
arrowheads — arrowheads read as PowerPoint). Data labels ON the marks. Footnotes live at the
bottom of their own panel, never a global footer paragraph.

**Number formatting conventions:** EPA signed, two decimals (`+0.13`, `+0.00` — zero is never
`0` or `-0.00`); percentiles with correct ordinals (`93rd`, `4th`, `21st`); rates one decimal
with % (`47.2%`); points/drive two decimals (`2.41`); counts `13 / 8.9 exp`; never more
precision than the data earns.

**Axis minimalism:** strip every axis that does not carry information; distributions get bottom
spine only, 3–4 x-ticks max, no y-ticks (density axis is meaningless to readers); bar rows
have no y-axis; scatterplots keep both axes, thin ticks, 4–5 ticks per axis; gridlines
horizontal only, faint, and only when they help read values.

**Layout rhythm:** one hero, then descending density; alternate panel heights and internal
texture; takeaways live ON the charts; every panel earns its rectangle (8 panels is the
ceiling; seven is better if one is weak); asymmetry signals importance; the scroll test —
export, scale to 390px wide, check the hero is readable without zooming, exactly one takeaway
per panel legible at a glance, no text block exceeds two lines; a panel that needs zooming is
too dense — cut a metric, not the font size. Fair-line delta drawn as a small visual in the
footer (market vs model line as two ticks on a number line, gap shaded Signal and labeled
`+1.5`), max two lines of type. Header: `GSE EDGE SHEET` kicker tracked mist, `WEEK 2 · 2026`
Signal, `BILLS vs LIONS` Cond Black 88–96pt (`vs` in Signal), one-line dateline fog 22pt, 4px
Signal rule, market chip `BUF -5.5` right. Footer: tagline `WE DETECT. YOU DECIDE.` tracked
Cond Bold 20pt + `@GalaxySportsHQ`; bottom hairline `DATA: NFLVERSE (CC-BY 4.0)` mono 14pt mist.

**Typography:** Display/headlines — Noto Sans Display Condensed (CondensedBlack for title,
Cond Bold for panel titles, ExtraBold for hero numbers), loaded in matplotlib via explicit
`FontProperties(fname=...)`; body/labels/data — Liberation Sans; mono accents — DejaVu Sans
Mono (data-source footer, tabular readouts). Tracked caps for panel titles and header kicker
(fake letter-spacing by joining chars with spaces; panel titles only, never body). **Do not
use:** DejaVu Sans for headlines (the Linux-default tell).

**The 16-item DO NOT LIST (hard bans, not suggestions):** (1) no pie or donut charts, ever;
(2) no radar/spider charts (angle distortion; percentile bar field does the job honestly;
fastest "AI generated this" tell); (3) no 3D effects, bevels, gradients, glows, drop shadows
(`FancyBboxPatch` gets facecolor and edgecolor only; `shadow=True` and glow path_effects
banned); (4) no dual y-axes (two scales on one chart is a lie waiting to happen; small
multiples instead); (5) no truncated bar axes that exaggerate gaps (percentile tracks run
0–100 always; if a gap looks small at honest scale, the gap IS small — say so); (6) no
rainbow categorical palettes (Bone, Signal, fog; the 30-team cloud is one gray; a fourth
color must be justified in build notes); (7) no legends where direct labeling works; (8) no
tick-label soup (if all 32 team abbreviations appear on any axis, delete that axis); (9) no
gridlines on scatterplots, no heavy box spines anywhere (hairline `#1E2128` dividers only);
(10) no orphan numbers; (11) no paragraph text (the v1 "THE READ" block does not come back in
any form); (12) no em dashes, no "sports intelligence," no hashtag walls, no AI-voice
adjectives; (13) no DejaVu Sans headlines; (14) no fake precision; (15) no overlapping text
on data (collisions visible at 390px are ship-blockers); (16) do not touch the v1 script or
PNG, do not edit the repo AGENTS.md, no git push, no external sends.

**Builder's pre-flight / environment quirk:** as of 2026-09-17 the system Python's matplotlib
import is BROKEN (`ImportError: numpy.core.multiarray failed to import`; system numpy 2.5.3 vs
numpy-1.x-compiled matplotlib). Before writing chart code, create a fresh venv and confirm
`import matplotlib` works — do not fight the system install.

**Instance facts (BUF vs LIONS, Week 2 2026, posted to @GalaxySportsHQ 2026-09-17 15:04 CDT):**
Bills vs Lions, 7:15 PM CT, New Highmark Stadium; market line BUF −5.5. Build scripts
`build_edge_sheet.py` / `build_edge_sheet_v2.py` in the same directory; final graphic
`bills-lions-edge-sheet-final-v2.png`. Sibling critiques: `DESIGN_CRITIQUES_V2.md`.
